result: The collapse of the illusion of separation. Not enforced harmony, not a single doctrine, but the quiet unraveling of the boundary that makes it possible to treat other minds, other generations, other ecosystems, or the future itself as abstract, disposable, or fundamentally apart from yourself. When interdependence is perceived as a lived reality—not a slogan, not an intellectual concept, but a structural truth—the internal logic of exploitation, hoarding, short-term extraction, and systemic indifference loses its footing. Conflict wouldn't vanish, nor would responsibility, but the ground from which all systems are built would shift. The rest would follow, unevenly, as it always does.
